promise-drhorton-1250-homes-agreement-20.title: Promise Robotics signs D.R. Horton agreement for more than 1,250 homes
promise-drhorton-1250-homes-agreement-20.summary: A multi-year agreement gives the homebuilder access to robotic production capacity without building its own factories.

sections.heading: A multi-year production agreement
paragraphs: Promise Robotics announced a commercial agreement with D.R. Horton to support production of more than 1,250 homes through Factory-as-a-Service. Promise calls it the first major US homebuilder on the platform as its US factory network expands.

sections.heading: Connecting designs with production
paragraphs: The platform converts existing home designs into production plans and robot instructions, then coordinates manufacturing, factory operations and site installation. Builders gain access to capacity without developing and operating their own automated factories.

sections.heading: Delivery results remain to be measured
paragraphs: The aim is greater capacity and more predictable cycles amid labour constraints. The agreed home count is not a completed-build count; the release provides neither project-level delivery schedules nor independently verified cost savings.

scan-olo-browser-robotics-partnership-20.title: Scan and OLO partner on browser-based Unitree robot deployment
scan-olo-browser-robotics-partnership-20.summary: The partnership combines hardware and AI infrastructure with browser tools for teleoperation, simulation and navigation.

sections.heading: Hardware meets deployment software
paragraphs: Scan Computers and Sheffield-based OLO Robotics are combining Scan’s robots, AI infrastructure and technical services with OLO’s browser platform. Target applications include industrial inspection, research and prototyping.

sections.heading: Test before deployment
paragraphs: Built on ROS 2, OLO brings together teleoperation, simulation, sensor monitoring and autonomous navigation. Teams can develop and test behaviour virtually before deploying it on Unitree robots supplied by Scan, using browser-based tools.

sections.heading: A lower starting barrier
paragraphs: The partners aim to reduce the initial dependence on specialist ROS developers, not prove that every installation needs no engineering. No measured deployment times or safety results are reported. A demonstration is planned at Scan booth 3068 at GTC Berlin, October 20–22.

yyforce-novotel-mercure-service-robot-ro.title: YYForce plans service robots at two Singapore on Stevens hotels
yyforce-novotel-mercure-service-robot-ro.summary: Deliveries, cleaning and concierge support come first; humanoid housekeeping remains a later research programme.

sections.heading: A two-hotel operating environment
paragraphs: YYForce, Novotel Singapore on Stevens and Mercure Singapore on Stevens announced a partnership across 772 guestrooms, restaurants and event spaces. The service-robot rollout is confirmed, but the release explicitly says deployment has not begun.

sections.heading: Prepare the building interfaces
paragraphs: Phase one covers specialist robots for guest deliveries, food-and-beverage transport, scheduled cleaning and concierge directions. Lift integration, routes, networking and arrival notifications must be prepared, with tasks matched to capability and technical readiness.

sections.heading: Savings are projections
paragraphs: A pre-deployment model projects roughly 10% lower monthly costs in selected operations, including robot costs; this is not a measured outcome. Later research would use permitted observations of housekeeping and banquet work, not establish autonomous cleaning of occupied guestrooms.

dominion-tencore-canadian-termit-product.title: Dominion and TENCORE plan Canadian TerMIT production for 2027
dominion-tencore-canadian-termit-product.summary: An MoU covers manufacturing transfer and AuraNet integration; definitive agreements remain to be completed.

sections.heading: An initial memorandum
paragraphs: Ottawa-based Dominion Dynamics and Ukraine’s TENCORE signed an MoU to manufacture TerMIT uncrewed ground vehicles in Canada and integrate Dominion’s AuraNet. The AUSA 2026 signing in Washington targets initial production in 2027.

sections.heading: Manufacturing transfer and training
paragraphs: A TENCORE team will lead technology transfer and train Canadian technicians. TENCORE reports delivering more than 5,000 UGVs to Ukrainian units since 2024; that historical figure is not a new order or delivery commitment under this MoU.

sections.heading: Plans still require execution
paragraphs: The partners intend to add AuraNet onboard and pursue an Arctic-capable version. Definitive agreements remain outstanding, so the announcement does not establish an operating Canadian line, new delivery volumes or test results for the combined system.

dynamic-creatures-hugo-43-actuator-demo-.title: Dynamic Creatures shows Hugo, a character robot with 43 actuators
dynamic-creatures-hugo-43-actuator-demo-.summary: The new video illustrates its hospitality ambitions; unsupervised guest interaction remains unproven.

sections.heading: A mobile guest-facing character
paragraphs: Dynamic Creatures released a Hugo video on October 12, showing a purple furry robot raising a hand and moving through an office. The company describes 43 actuators combined with character design and expressive movement for entertainment and hospitality.

sections.heading: Expression remains in development
paragraphs: Its Vision-Language-Expression model is being developed to connect perception and language with gestures, movement and emotional expression. Navigation and close-contact safety are also described as work in progress, not fully established capabilities.

sections.heading: Autonomy and hardware are unconfirmed
paragraphs: A development-screen image resembles a modified Unitree G1, but the company has not confirmed that identification. Its earlier Boston Dynamics partnership does not identify Hugo’s hardware either. The clip provides no intervention rate or sustained guest-operation results.

google-argon-apollo-cornhole-sim-feedbac.summary: Seven consecutive successful throws follow practice and physical feedback, rather than demonstrating a first-attempt success rate.

sections.heading: From observation to simulation
paragraphs: Google showed Gemini 4 Argon observing a human cornhole video, helping construct a MuJoCo environment and refining movement before transfer to Apptronik’s Apollo. The company demonstrated seven consecutive successful throws.

sections.heading: Physical feedback is part of the process
paragraphs: The account includes stance, swing and release adjustments using bag landing positions on real hardware. The streak supplies neither the total attempt count nor the human engineering effort, so it cannot establish general accuracy or first-attempt success.

sections.heading: Keep generated plans separate
paragraphs: Another linked demonstration uses Argon to iteratively steer Gemini Omni video toward spelling ARGON; it is a generated plan, not evidence of that physical task. The reported 87% ERQA score is an image-and-text reasoning result, not an 87% robot task-success rate.

robros-korea-20-robot-industrial-sandbox.title: South Korea clears a 20-robot Robros industrial trial
robros-korea-20-robot-industrial-sandbox.summary: The sandbox permits testing near workers with risk controls; it is not a completed factory-performance result.

sections.heading: Permission for real-site testing
paragraphs: Seoul Economic Daily reports that South Korea granted Robros a regulatory-sandbox exemption to trial 20 humanoids at manufacturing and logistics sites. This authorizes testing; it does not establish that all robots are deployed or have passed performance tests.

sections.heading: Four industrial settings
paragraphs: The named sites are Nepes, Sungwoo Hitech, HD Hyundai Samho and Delivery Lab. Planned tasks include cleaning semiconductor-packaging components, positioning vehicle body parts, stacking shipbuilding support components and moving refrigerated logistics containers.

sections.heading: Evidence for future safety standards
paragraphs: Work near people requires risk assessment and mitigation, with trial evidence intended to inform future standards. Robros’s separate AI roadmap for the first half of 2027 does not establish that the future model powers this trial or that these tasks already run autonomously.

hylight-13m-airship-inspection-funding-2.title: HyLight raises €13 million to expand autonomous inspection airships
hylight-13m-airship-inspection-funding-2.summary: The company targets a fleet increase from four to 15 while expanding AI analysis and European operations.

sections.heading: Funding inspection services
paragraphs: French company HyLight raised €13 million from Rubio Impact Ventures, DRW and Teampact Ventures alongside existing investors. Its hydrogen-powered airships inspect power lines, pipelines and railways, with a target of 15 aircraft by 2027 versus four today.

sections.heading: Endurance and sensing
paragraphs: The 12-metre HyLighter is specified for up to ten hours of flight and ten kilograms of sensors, including LiDAR, cameras and methane detectors. The company says its analysis locates vegetation risks and more than 50 types of power-grid defects.

sections.heading: Scaling an integrated service
paragraphs: HyLight builds and operates its aircraft and supplies analysis to customers including Enedis, NaTran, Téréga, SNCF Réseau and VINCI. Funding supports manufacturing, hiring and markets such as Germany and the Netherlands; 15 aircraft remains a target and flights require applicable permissions.

elsight-halo-cellular-positioning-launch.title: Elsight introduces cellular positioning for Halo
elsight-halo-cellular-positioning-launch.summary: The feature combines multiple inputs when GPS fails and checks satellite positions against cellular-derived location.

sections.heading: A software-enabled Halo feature
paragraphs: Elsight announced Positioning on October 12 for uncrewed air, ground and maritime systems. Existing Halo customers can enable it through software without additional hardware; new customers still need Halo as the base platform.

sections.heading: Combine cellular and other inputs
paragraphs: The system derives location from cellular network measurements and fuses base-station, motion and trusted GPS inputs. Elsight describes spoofing detection that compares GPS with cellular-derived position and alerts when the difference exceeds a threshold.

sections.heading: Validate the operating environment
paragraphs: The vendor says internet access and visual references are unnecessary, but the method still relies on available cellular measurements. No environment-specific accuracy figures or independent test results are supplied; coverage and behaviour with insufficient inputs remain evaluation questions.

monopulse-over2m-production-funding-2026.title: Monopulse raises more than €2 million for production and R&D
monopulse-over2m-production-funding-2026.summary: The investment supports manufacturing and market expansion alongside work on resilience to disrupted communications and navigation.

sections.heading: Capital for manufacturing growth
paragraphs: MNP Technologijos, trading as Monopulse, raised more than €2 million from Lithuanian and international investors. Participants include Coinvest Capital, Plug and Play, LitBAN and an NGL Ventures syndicate contributing €560,000 from 68 investors.

sections.heading: Hardware and software development
paragraphs: The Danish-Lithuanian company develops Falcon MK3S and HydroHex systems, combining electronics, sensor fusion, computer vision and AI. Maintaining communication or autonomous operation when signals are disrupted is a development focus, not a guarantee against every interference condition.

sections.heading: Watch production and delivery
paragraphs: Tech.eu reports existing use by Lithuanian and Danish armed forces. The investment supports manufacturing, R&D and expansion in Scandinavia and other international markets, without specifying added unit capacity or independently comparable resilience results.

piab-ps-series-vacuum-sensors-launch-202.title: Piab launches PS Series vacuum sensors for automated handling
piab-ps-series-vacuum-sensors-launch-202.summary: Three variants span analog monitoring, switching and IO-Link, with NFC setup for supported switches.

sections.heading: Feedback at the handling point
paragraphs: Piab introduced the PS Series on October 14 to expose vacuum levels, switching status and operating feedback close to the application. The range is intended to help automated vacuum handling respond to changing conditions.

sections.heading: Three connection options
paragraphs: PS.VA provides continuous analog monitoring. PS.VS combines digital switching and analog output, while PS.VSI adds IO-Link for integration into automation systems needing richer digital feedback.

sections.heading: Phone-based commissioning
paragraphs: The Piab Connect app uses NFC to adjust settings, copy configurations and read statistics on supported switches. Easier commissioning is the intended benefit; the announcement provides neither pricing nor field-test reductions in handling failures.

dji-dock4-matrice5td-battery-swap-launch.title: DJI launches Dock 4 with 25-second automatic battery swaps
dji-dock4-matrice5td-battery-swap-launch.summary: The Matrice 5TD pairing targets shorter gaps between emergency-response and inspection flights.

sections.heading: Less turnaround between missions
paragraphs: DJI launched Dock 4 with the Matrice 5TD, claiming a 25-second automatic battery swap instead of an approximately 30-minute recharge. The drone’s stated maximum endurance is 59 minutes, targeting response teams and scheduled inspections.

sections.heading: Multiple sensing systems
paragraphs: Matrice 5TD combines telephoto, infrared and night imaging with laser ranging. Three-direction mmWave radar, rotating LiDAR and six-direction vision support obstacle detection. An O4 Ground Station can improve communications around obstructions.

sections.heading: Performance has conditions
paragraphs: DJI specifies a −40°C to 50°C operating range for Dock 4 and sales through Enterprise dealers. Performance figures come from controlled testing; some features depend on paired equipment and region, requiring deployment-specific checks.

fort-connectivity-aggregation-launch-202.title: FORT launches Connectivity Aggregation for robotic communications
fort-connectivity-aggregation-launch-202.summary: The software combines cellular, satellite, Wi-Fi and radio links and can run on customer hardware.

sections.heading: Reducing single-network dependence
paragraphs: FORT Robotics introduced Connectivity Aggregation at AUSA on October 14. It combines different connections into one adaptive link to preserve visibility and control over autonomous or remotely operated machines when a network degrades.

sections.heading: Flexible integration
paragraphs: The software supports public and private cellular, satellite, Wi-Fi and radio networks. FORT says proprietary devices or custom cellular links are unnecessary: customers can use their own hardware, deploy it independently or integrate its wider platform.

sections.heading: Rollout is not a universal guarantee
paragraphs: FORT reports an active rollout with several defence customers and offers integration support. No independently verified latency or availability measurements accompany the announcement, so uninterrupted operation in every environment is not established.

agility-s4-effective-november2-vote-2026.summary: The Nasdaq transaction advances, while financing and completion remain conditional.

sections.heading: The next transaction milestone
paragraphs: Agility says the S-4 for its Churchill Capital Corp XI combination became effective on October 13. Churchill XI shareholders will vote on November 2. Closing is expected in November, followed by a Nasdaq listing as AGLT.

sections.heading: Expected financing
paragraphs: Projected gross proceeds exceed $620 million, including roughly $424 million in trust assuming no redemptions and about $200 million in a Foxconn-led PIPE. Agility intends to support orders, deployments and Digit 5 production.

sections.heading: Completion remains conditional
paragraphs: An effective registration statement is not investment endorsement or a completed transaction. Shareholder approval and other conditions remain. This is a new financing milestone distinct from Digit 5’s launch, not evidence that all funds or robots have been delivered.

boston-dynamics-atlas-prototype-build-ti.summary: A prototype-shop video describes roughly one-day builds today and closer links between machining, assembly and engineering.

sections.heading: Inside prototype operations
paragraphs: A new Boston Dynamics film shows Atlas teams combining construction, testing, maintenance and repair. Senior technical programme manager Katie Conner describes roughly one-day robot builds today and an ambition for approximately an hour next year.

sections.heading: Machining close to engineering
paragraphs: Keeping precision work such as gear cutting in-house lets engineers discuss changes directly with machinists. Staff describe some parts reaching assembly the same or next day, alongside process development and robotic arms used in assembly.

sections.heading: Build time is not shipment throughput
paragraphs: The hour is a target, not an achieved result, and the film does not establish a shipment rate. Faster prototype work can accelerate hardware iteration, but its process boundaries must be understood before comparisons with other production lines.

physical-intelligence-api-beta-launch-20.summary: Developers can fine-tune on PI-managed infrastructure and access hosted inference, with admission in batches.

sections.heading: Managed training infrastructure
paragraphs: Physical Intelligence announced its API beta on October 13. Teams upload demonstrations, fine-tune using PI-managed compute and access models through a hosted inference gateway, reducing infrastructure work for robot developers.

sections.heading: Iteration still needs real data
paragraphs: Developers must test on hardware and collect new examples around failures. PI cites Almond’s dual-arm Axol deburring its own assembly spacers after four days of API iteration; this does not establish a four-day training time for every task.

sections.heading: Limited initial access
paragraphs: The beta starts small and requires an application. Most demonstrations used cloud inference, with connectivity challenges in some applications. Questions about local inference in the application form do not establish availability of a local deployment service.

toro-haven-am75-2027-mower-announcement-.title: Toro announces HAVEN AM75 robotic mower for 2027
toro-haven-am75-2027-mower-announcement-.summary: LiDAR navigation and app-defined boundaries target properties of up to three-quarters of an acre.

sections.heading: A residential robot for 2027
paragraphs: Toro announced HAVEN AM75 for properties up to three-quarters of an acre, using LiDAR navigation and camera obstacle detection. Dealer, website and retail availability starts in 2027, rather than immediate delivery.

sections.heading: Mapping the lawn
paragraphs: Automatic mapping detects grass edges. Where boundaries are unclear, users steer the mower through an app to define them and create exclusion zones. It is designed to cross paths between lawn areas and includes rain sensors.

sections.heading: Information still needed

paragraphs: The platform generates 3D Gaussian Splatting, mesh and depth data, with object segmentation and AI filling of unscanned areas. It supports Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab. Hesai estimates 15 minutes to scan a typical 100-square-metre room, depending on layout.

sections.heading: Specifications and reported results
paragraphs: Maximum capture is 8K, but exported files top out at 6K. Hesai cites a DQ deployment with 99% Sharpa task success and much faster scene preparation. Those vendor-reported case results are not a general benchmark or guarantee.

tieriv-taisei-autoflow-three-vehicle-tri.summary: An eight-day demonstration will test coordinated autonomous traffic and simpler infrastructure for dedicated logistics lanes.

sections.heading: An eight-day demonstration
paragraphs: Taisei, TIER IV and Taisei Rotec were selected for Japan’s MLIT Autoflow Road programme, which envisages unmanned cargo vehicles in dedicated lanes. Three vehicles will run for eight days in late October–early November at a full-scale tunnel facility and test track.

sections.heading: Testing shared operating space
paragraphs: Planned checks include following, opposing traffic, lane changes, merging, obstacle avoidance and berth stopping accuracy at different lane widths. Pilot.Auto, based on Autoware, will be evaluated alongside T-Localizer and roadside infrastructure.

sections.heading: Test vehicles are not final transporters
paragraphs: The passenger-car-based vehicles are experimental, not final logistics hardware. Building on fiscal-2025 work, this round evaluates multiple vehicles and simpler sensor arrangements. Results from the new trial are not yet available.

sections.heading: Learning through simulation
paragraphs: Detailed physics simulation and demonstrations teach tasks instead of fixed scripts. Stations can be reconfigured and redeployed. The founders report smartphone applications including flex-cable handling and film peeling, but do not identify that customer.

sections.heading: BMW results are still outstanding
paragraphs: The company claims changeovers in minutes rather than weeks. The article provides no BMW measurements or independent validation. The partnership is an evaluation, not confirmation of a factory-wide rollout or fully autonomous end-to-end car production.

Interchangeable tools apply compound, sand and prime walls, with feedback-based force control maintaining sanding pressure. Its Construction Action Model connects planning, an action policy and control, using simulation and job-site data.

sections.heading: Scaling remains the test
paragraphs: The target is 150 deployed robots by the end of 2027, with drywall installation, drilling and conduit work planned later. Crews still map sites and replenish materials. sections.heading: A shared autonomy layer

sections.heading: Further development ahead

sections.heading: The work behind autonomous trips
paragraphs: Element Mobility will coordinate staff, facilities, infrastructure and vehicle readiness. Maintenance, charging, energy management, cleaning and fleet data are included. This announcement concerns fleet operations rather than a new version of the driving system.

sections.heading: A future timetable
paragraphs: The partners expect to create hundreds of roles over time, including maintenance, validation driving and customer service. paragraphs: FF EAI Robotics and Faraday Future introduced Nova for developers and educators at $2,490, with a $390 Developer Skills Package. Nova Mini costs $299, while its accompanying curriculum costs $499. Device prices therefore need to be distinguished from additional learning products.

Development support includes an SDK, a ROS 2 workflow and reinforcement learning through NVIDIA Isaac before policies are tested on hardware.

sections.heading: A phased release
paragraphs: The first phase is limited to 100 invited buyers, with the first 20 units described as ready for immediate delivery. Applicants must be selected before ordering; broader developer and consumer releases follow later. Mini targets ages eight and up with block programming. sections.heading: Identifying the battery partner
paragraphs: Agility Robotics named Nyobolt as the battery technology provider for Digit 5, a new energy partnership following the robot’s introduction. It targets warehouses, distribution centers and manufacturing operators seeking less charging downtime between shifts.

sections.heading: A ten-to-one operating ratio
paragraphs: The companies specify 90 minutes of runtime and a nine-minute recharge, a 10:1 ratio compared with Digit 4’s 2:1. They project more than 20 working hours per day. These are company performance claims; the release does not disclose pack capacity or detailed long-term cycle-test results.

sections.heading: Access expected next year
paragraphs: Early access to Digit 5 with this technology is expected in the first half of 2027, with availability increasing over the following six to nine months. tieriv-tum-autoware-research-center-2026.title: TIER IV and TUM establish an Autoware research center
tieriv-tum-autoware-research-center-2026.summary: Three research groups will combine learning-based driving with rule-based supervision and shared evaluation methods.

sections.heading: A long-term research base
paragraphs: TIER IV and the Technical University of Munich established the TUM Autoware Research Center by TIER IV through a multi-year collaboration funded by the company. FTM, CPS and AVS groups will advance open autonomous-driving software, doctoral training and links between research and deployment.

sections.heading: Three technical priorities
paragraphs: Safety work will pair deep-learning driving models with rule-based supervision that intervenes against defined constraints. Evaluation will cover components and whole systems in simulation, offline analysis and real vehicles. Scalability work will create repeatable processes for adapting Autoware to new environments.

sections.heading: Building on earlier work
paragraphs: The center builds on EDGAR and CommonRoad expertise. EDGAR’s IAA MOBILITY 2025 demonstrations predate the center and are not results of this new initiative. No funding amount or new safety-guardian test results are disclosed; improvements will be contributed to open source where appropriate.

neura-neuron-ai-multisensory-launch-2026.title: NEURA introduces Neuron AI with touch, sound and memory
neura-neuron-ai-multisensory-launch-2026.summary: The locally running model is set for an eleven-minute laundry-handling demonstration at GTC Berlin.

sections.heading: Perception beyond cameras
paragraphs: NEURA announced Neuron AI on October 14, with Humanoids Daily reporting the details the next day. Its Perception-Language-Action model combines 3D vision, force and touch, audio, robot state and language with memory, targeting tasks such as recognizing that a component has locked into place.

sections.heading: Training and local execution
paragraphs: The company identifies five embodiments: 4NE1 generations 3 and 4, a wheeled version and two further bimanual platforms. Training combines physical robot data, simulation and sensor-suit demonstrations. Inference runs on the robot without requiring the cloud, while Neuraverse is intended to support customer-specific skill adaptation.

sections.heading: An upcoming demonstration
paragraphs: At GTC Berlin on October 20–22, NEURA plans an eleven-minute sequence spanning laundry sorting, washer loading and transfer to a dryer. That duration covers handling rather than a full wash-and-dry cycle. The announcement provides no repeated-run success rate, intervention count or measured Time-to-Skill result.

120ft-576k-container-microfactory-launch.summary: The three-container concept targets small assembly batches, with brands paying for completed products.

sections.heading: A shared small factory
paragraphs: Stockholm startup 120ft disclosed €576,000 from 22 angel investors to develop humanoid-operated assembly facilities in three 40-foot containers. They divide preparation, assembly, and inspection with packing. The company plans to own and operate the facilities while customers pay per finished product.

sections.heading: Starting with constrained work
paragraphs: The proposed service starts at batches of 100, with brands retaining designs and component suppliers. Initial pilots target rigid parts below 5 kg joined by screws or press-fits; cables, flexible materials and gluing come later. Factory OS is intended to connect AI, robots and automation to assembly workflows.

sections.heading: Programming time is not cycle time
paragraphs: The company says skill-programming time fell from seven weeks in 2025 to seven hours in 2026, with seven minutes targeted for 2027. Its curve is an outlook rather than measured time-series data, and does not describe manufacturing time per item. Success rates and human-assistance frequency remain undisclosed, leaving commercial quality and economics to be demonstrated.

sections.heading: Open to international teams
paragraphs: MassRobotics opened applications for cohort six of its Healthcare Robotics Startup Catalyst Program from October 15 through December 31, 2026. The non-equity program runs from February to June 2027 and welcomes early and more mature teams worldwide, including Seed through Series C companies.

sections.heading: Mentoring around practical milestones
paragraphs: Intel joins Festo, Novanta and Mitsubishi Electric US on the steering committee, adding edge-AI and on-device computing expertise. Teams receive technical mentoring and clinical perspectives, with biweekly mentor sessions supporting prototypes, pilot design, regulatory planning or systems integration.

sections.heading: Fit and selection
paragraphs: Eligible areas include laboratories, pharmaceuticals, diagnostics, hospital logistics, rehabilitation and surgical robotics. Selection considers technical maturity, clinical relevance and achievable near-term milestones. The program has mentored 35 startups since 2021, but that record is neither medical approval nor a funding guarantee for new participants.

sections.heading: Assistance and remote presence
paragraphs: Devanthro has become Plim Robotics. Its proposed home robot combines AI assistance with remote operation, allowing relatives or caregivers to appear on its face display and interact through its body. The company advertises operation across distances up to 9,000 km.

sections.heading: Published specifications

sections.heading: Performance remains unquantified
paragraphs: Families and care organizations can register interest, but pricing, delivery dates and household task-success rates remain undisclosed. Two hours of battery life does not imply all-day operation without charging, and the frequency of human intervention is unknown.

sections.heading: Flexibility is the application

sections.heading: A reusable skill library
paragraphs: ASPIRE version 1.0 provides an agent framework for discovering and refining robot skills, storing reusable knowledge in a skill library. Its GitHub project lists new Rubik’s Cube capability and real-robot learning.

sections.heading: Scores have a defined scope
paragraphs: The team reports about 99% on 80 LIBERO-Pro tasks and 100% on seven representative Robosuite tasks and two BEHAVIOR-1K tasks after switching to GPT-6 Astra. These are simulation scores, not universal real-world robot success rates.

sections.heading: Open code and hardware questions

dsp-supervised-play-world-model-preprint.title: DSP uses supervised play to bootstrap robot interaction and planning
dsp-supervised-play-world-model-preprint.summary: The research links human play, autonomous data collection and a world model, while its early hardware evaluation remains provisional.

sections.heading: Learning how to interact
paragraphs: Dexterity from Supervised Play, or DSP, first imitates human object interaction without a specific final task goal. The resulting play policy then collects additional autonomous interaction data to train a world model.

sections.heading: Predicting before acting
paragraphs: Given a goal, the play policy proposes action sequences and the world model predicts their outcomes for model-predictive control. The paper also proposes distilling a policy through play inside the learned model to reduce inference cost.

sections.heading: Hardware conclusions remain provisional
paragraphs: The paper studies object pushing and in-hand reorientation, but its first-version conclusion describes hardware results as provisional and calls for a frozen protocol and uncertainty estimates. Headline gains should therefore not be treated as settled hardware comparisons.

paragraphs: An October 19 video shows KAIST Humanoid v0.9 pushing objects weighing up to 35 kg and lifting up to 20 kg while arranging objects into the letters KAIST. DRCD Lab developed the platform with RAILAB, which developed its arms.

sections.heading: Coordinating contact and balance
paragraphs: Physical handling requires coordinated locomotion and contact: force applied through the arms changes the demands on the legs and torso. The team reports onboard visual feedback and interaction skills learned through deep reinforcement learning and human demonstrations. The video description does not fully explain how those components are combined.

sections.heading: Pushing and lifting are different measures
paragraphs: Pushing a 35 kg object does not require supporting its full weight, and resistance depends on surface conditions. That result must be separated from the 20 kg lift. The demonstration is neither a commercial payload rating nor evidence of unrestricted autonomy, and it does not establish durability under repeated production work.

sections.heading: Model access through an API
paragraphs: Dream Labs emerged with $90 million in seed funding led by B Capital and Kindred Ventures and opened Dream API to connect observations and language instructions to robot actions. Its technical documentation prices Dream-1 inference at $3 per hour and the flash version at $2. Those figures are not the purchase or total operating cost of a robot.

sections.heading: A shared gripper-level interface
paragraphs: The technical explanation describes predicting end-effector poses and gripper opening, then using each robot’s inverse-kinematics solver to produce joint commands. This supports transfer among bimanual parallel-gripper robots, using a head camera and two wrist cameras. It should not be interpreted as immediate support for every robot architecture.

sections.heading: Demonstrations have boundaries
paragraphs: Examples include manipulation and laundry folding, but the company acknowledges dependence on IK quality, workspace and mechanical differences. A fine-tuning service uses robot-specific data when zero-shot performance is insufficient. Dream-1 remains a research beta that can make mistakes and has not been validated for safety-critical use.

paragraphs: Its LaserWeeder G2 is pulled behind a tractor and uses AI to detect and map plants before targeting weeds with lasers. Founded in 2018, Carbon Robotics has raised about $177 million. sections.heading: Do not infer product changes without evidence
paragraphs: The report documents a cost adjustment at an agricultural robotics supplier. nvidia-flora-data-engine-public-disclosu.title: NVIDIA details Flora’s video-annotation pipeline for robot learning
nvidia-flora-data-engine-public-disclosu.summary: The system segments actions, writes captions and evaluates execution, with throughput reported across 512 GPUs.

sections.heading: A public account of the GR00T data engine
paragraphs: NVIDIA researchers introduced Flora publicly on October 20, followed by Humanoids Daily’s report the next day. It prepares human and robot video for GR00T. The Rewarder card dates its model-file release to October 15, so this covers the system overview and performance disclosure rather than claiming every file first appeared today.

sections.heading: Separating intent from outcome
paragraphs: TempSeg divides footage into action intervals, Captioner describes the attempted operation and Rewarder assesses execution quality or success. A failed grasp can therefore retain its intended-action label without treating failure as the goal. Outputs are learning annotations, not motor commands.

sections.heading: Cluster throughput and usage limits
paragraphs: NVIDIA reports annotating 200,000 video hours daily with 512 GB300 GPUs, not collecting that much new robot experience or training time. Captioner and Rewarder cards restrict intended use to noncommercial research and development. Published comparisons show both stronger and weaker results across individual metrics.

humanoid-nvidia-single-computer-architec.title: Humanoid expands NVIDIA work to consolidate two onboard computers into one
humanoid-nvidia-single-computer-architec.summary: Jetson Thor and sensor-processing tools target simpler computing and control in the company’s next-generation robots.

sections.heading: An onboard architecture update
paragraphs: UK robotics company Humanoid announced an expanded NVIDIA collaboration on October 21. It says moving to Jetson Thor consolidates two onboard computers into one while maintaining computing capacity, aiming to support more sophisticated AI in its next generation of robots.

sections.heading: A shorter sensor-to-model path
paragraphs: Shared CPU and GPU memory reduces data movement, while Holoscan Sensor Bridge can place camera data directly in GPU-accessible memory. Humanoid is integrating Holoscan SDK and Isaac OS to coordinate perception, inference and control workloads on a common platform.

sections.heading: System-level results remain undisclosed
paragraphs: The work extends existing Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab use and does not replace Humanoid’s KinetIQ AI framework. End-to-end latency, energy savings, task-success changes and a next-generation launch date are not disclosed. Fewer computers should therefore be distinguished from measured performance gains.

generative-bionics-amd-data-factory-plan.summary: The first of three planned sites targets Q4 2027, linking real industrial practice with digital-twin simulation.

sections.heading: A proposed three-site network
paragraphs: Generative Bionics announced its Physical AI Data Factory plan on October 21. A 5,000-square-meter Italian hub targets Q4 2027, followed by another European site and a third serving global markets. The city, investment budget and timing of later facilities are not specified.

sections.heading: Real practice and simulation form a loop
paragraphs: The sites would recreate industrial settings for GENE.01 to collect vision, motion, force and tactile data. Digital twins would then vary objects and conditions before trained models return to physical robots for validation. The cycle aims to prepare robots before customer deployment.

sections.heading: AMD supplies the planned compute foundation
paragraphs: AMD Helios is intended for model training, physical and synthetic data processing and parallel simulations, without disclosed installation size or robot count. The accompanying image is a concept illustration. This remains planned infrastructure, not an operating facility or established industrial validation result.

peraso-60ghz-humanoid-edge-validation-20.title: Peraso validates a 60 GHz humanoid-to-edge link at about 500 Mbps uplink
peraso-60ghz-humanoid-edge-validation-20.summary: The demonstration keeps urgent responses on a local GPU while a remote cluster handles more demanding models.

sections.heading: Wireless link validation
paragraphs: Peraso announced a functional validation on October 21 connecting a humanoid to an edge AI server over 60 GHz wireless. It reports sustained throughput of approximately 500 Mbps from robot to server and 100 Mbps in the reverse direction for video, sensors and operational data.

sections.heading: Splitting local and remote computation
paragraphs: The demonstration uses a local NVIDIA GPU for urgent, low-latency responses and a remote GPU cluster for more demanding models. This reduces the need to run every model onboard, while system design must still address connectivity limitations.

sections.heading: The demonstration has a defined scope
paragraphs: Directional beamforming is intended to reduce interference between nearby links. A separately cited 50 Gbps aggregate result came from an earlier demonstration, not this robot’s link. End-to-end latency and long-term factory reliability results are not disclosed.

dexory-nvidia-halos-safety-testing-2026.title: Dexory tests NVIDIA Halos for warehouse robot safety architecture
dexory-nvidia-halos-safety-testing-2026.summary: The company is exploring an IGX Thor-based single-board approach before a planned worldwide fleet rollout.

sections.heading: Testing next-generation capabilities
paragraphs: Dexory announced on October 21 that it is testing NVIDIA Halos, which combines real-time AI, functional safety and edge computing through IGX Thor. The work targets warehouse robots operating alongside people, forklifts and other moving equipment.

sections.heading: Building on warehouse operations
paragraphs: DexoryView combines autonomous robot data and digital twins to describe inventory and warehouse space. The company is exploring a single-board architecture for broader perception and inside-out safety, building on its existing use of NVIDIA Cosmos for warehouse intelligence.

sections.heading: A rollout plan is not completed certification
paragraphs: Dexory plans to deploy the technology across its worldwide fleet but gives no start date or quantitative test results. Testing does not establish that every robot is upgraded or that a new safety certification is complete. Results remain dependent on development and validation.

robotiq-2fc-tactile-gripper-launch-2026.title: Robotiq launches 2FC tactile gripper with Q1 2027 shipping planned
robotiq-2fc-tactile-gripper-launch-2026.summary: The 85 mm and 140 mm versions combine sensing, AI Hub compute and Contact Core for data capture and local grasp control.

sections.heading: Preorders for a Physical AI gripper
paragraphs: Robotiq introduced 2FC on October 21 with 85 mm and 140 mm stroke versions available to preorder and shipping planned for Q1 2027. It builds on 2F with tactile sensors, wrist-mounted AI Hub compute and Contact Core software to use the same hardware for data collection and deployment.

sections.heading: Contact data and local responses
paragraphs: The gripper synchronizes pressure, vibration, proprioception, force, position and current at millisecond level. Robotiq describes onboard grasp-quality assessment, incipient-slip detection, object-pose estimation and centering, alongside planned ROS 2 and C++ development tools.

sections.heading: Upgrade options and specification limits
paragraphs: Existing 2F owners can add TSF sensors and AI Hub for Physical AI development without replacing the whole gripper. The stated two-million-cycle rating is not a guarantee of identical lifetime in every environment or perfect grasp success. Evaluation must account for actual objects and operating conditions.

nebius-workbench-cosmos-sereact-expansio.title: Nebius expands Physical AI Workbench with Cosmos Data Factory and Sereact workflows
nebius-workbench-cosmos-sereact-expansio.summary: AI agents can operate data, simulation, training and evaluation workflows, including a returns-handling sim-to-real pipeline.

sections.heading: An integration update for robotics development
paragraphs: On October 21, Nebius detailed the integration of NVIDIA Cosmos Data Factory into Physical AI Workbench, with workflows agents can read and operate across data generation, simulation, training and evaluation. Workbench was previously available; this update centers on integrations and expanded collaboration.

sections.heading: Connecting tools and infrastructure
paragraphs: Named components include Cosmos 3, Isaac Sim, Isaac Lab, Isaac GR00T and SONIC, alongside Genesis, Voxel51 and Foxglove for simulation, data and observability. The aim is to reduce manual integration by offering orchestrated workflows and GPU infrastructure that teams can adapt to their tasks.

sections.heading: Sereact collaboration and reported benefits
paragraphs: Nebius and Sereact are co-designing a sim-to-real pipeline for Zalando returns handling. Engineering-time reductions of up to 40% are customer reports presented by Nebius, not guaranteed results for every project. The framework is available on GitHub; compute resources still need to be provisioned for the workload.

avride-grubhub-wonder-four-market-expans.title: Avride expands Grubhub and Wonder robot delivery across four US markets
avride-grubhub-wonder-four-market-expans.summary: Philadelphia, Hoboken and Arlington County join a wider Jersey City service area, with restaurant and customer opt-in.

sections.heading: Expansion beyond the earlier pilot
paragraphs: Avride announced expanded Grubhub and Wonder delivery on October 21 across Philadelphia, Hoboken in New Jersey and Arlington County in Virginia, plus a larger Jersey City area following its earlier pilot. This is separate from Avride’s existing Uber Eats operation in Philadelphia.

sections.heading: Restaurants and customers opt in
paragraphs: Grubhub restaurants can choose robot delivery, while customers must opt in and be within a supported area. The plan includes Wonder food halls and other participating restaurants, with dozens expected to join across the four markets. It does not mean every order will travel by robot.

sections.heading: Fleet size remains undisclosed
paragraphs: Avride has not specified how many robots it will add in Philadelphia. The announcement establishes planned partner and geographic expansion rather than measured delivery-capacity or speed gains. Sharing sidewalks with people remains an important issue as the service grows.

yita-100m-yuan-seed-rounds-disclosure-20.title: YITA raises over RMB 100 million for force-controlled robot hardware
yita-100m-yuan-seed-rounds-disclosure-20.summary: Seed and seed-plus funding includes Galbot and Fourier, supporting a focus on arms and joint modules for embodied AI.

sections.heading: Combined early-stage funding
paragraphs: Chinese robot hardware startup YITA disclosed on October 20 that it had raised over RMB 100 million across seed and seed-plus rounds, with TechNode reporting the following day. The figure combines two rounds rather than describing a separate new single-round investment.

sections.heading: Arms and joints for controlled contact
paragraphs: Founded in May 2026, YITA develops force-controlled arms and high-performance joint modules. Its portfolio spans integrated actuators, compliant dual-arm systems and manipulation platforms, targeting hardware that lets embodied AI and humanoid developers regulate contact forces when handling objects.

sections.heading: Investors and remaining unknowns
paragraphs: Named investors include Galbot, Fourier, Matrix Partners China, CCB International, SenseTime Guoxiang Capital and the L2F founder fund. Lighthouse Capital is its incubator and exclusive financial adviser. The report does not supply force-control accuracy, shipment figures or customer-test results establishing readiness across its portfolio.

tesla-optimus-fremont-early-ramp-q3-2026.summary: The Q3 update confirms an early production ramp, while output figures remain undisclosed and hands, durability and AI need further work.

sections.heading: Manufacturing enters an early ramp
paragraphs: Tesla’s Q3 update says its Fremont Optimus line has started producing robots it calls production-quality. California is classified as an early ramp and Texas as construction. Current weekly output and cumulative production were not disclosed.

sections.heading: A training fleet remains a target
paragraphs: On the October 21 earnings call, Elon Musk described a need for roughly 10,000–20,000 robots to practice and generate experience in Optimus Academy. That is not a completed production total. Training combines human demonstrations with practice on physical robots and in simulation.

sections.heading: Commercial delivery still depends on development
paragraphs: Musk forecasts outside-company deliveries around late 2027, initially for industrial work. Hands, durability and AI behavior need refinement, with AI5 integration targeted around April 2027 if the program stays on schedule. These are forecasts; no household launch date or price was provided.

agile-one-sn-research-humanoid-launch-20.title: Agile Robots introduces Agile ONE SN research humanoid with 71 degrees of freedom
agile-one-sn-research-humanoid-launch-20.summary: Tactile hands, Jetson Thor and GR00T combine in a laboratory platform scheduled for early 2027.

sections.heading: A compact laboratory platform
paragraphs: Unveiled at GTC Berlin on October 21, Agile ONE SN is 1.4 meters tall, with 31 body degrees of freedom plus 20 in each Wuji hand, totaling 71. Payload is up to 3 kg per arm. Agile lists 43 kg while NVIDIA lists 40 kg, leaving the delivered specification worth checking.

sections.heading: Reducing integration before experiments
paragraphs: Jetson Thor, multi-view cameras and lidar accompany preconfigured GR00T 1.7 and whole-body control. Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab assets support demonstration capture, data generation, training, evaluation and physical testing. Researchers can integrate selected components with their existing stack.

sections.heading: Transfer and safety require validation
paragraphs: Agile intends skills and data to transfer to its larger industrial Agile ONE, but cross-body transfer needs task-specific validation. Availability is planned for early 2027. Halos integration remains exploratory, rather than proof of a fully implemented or certified safety platform.

signode-expanded-pallet-amr-portfolio-20.title: Signode expands pallet AMR portfolio to connect packaging and storage
signode-expanded-pallet-amr-portfolio-20.summary: Lifting robots, pallet trucks and forklift configurations extend material flow beyond end-of-line packaging.

sections.heading: More configurations for pallet handling
paragraphs: On October 22, Signode expanded its AMR portfolio with lifting robots, pallet trucks, counterbalanced forklifts, reach trucks and stacker forklifts. These move completed pallet loads between production, storage and distribution, with configurations selected for lifting and load requirements.

sections.heading: Connecting movement and storage
paragraphs: Signode says the robots navigate without fixed floor lines or magnetic strips and can reroute around obstructions. Deployments are designed to integrate warehouse and fleet-management software, including pallet delivery into StorFast ASRS to connect packaging, transport and storage.

sections.heading: Scaling fleets with demand
paragraphs: Customers can add capacity and capabilities over time. Signode cites one warehouse with more than 17 robots; its broader figure of over 800 vehicles across more than 80 locations is not a sales total for the new models. Individual prices and performance specifications were not detailed.

neura-tum-robogym-opening-4ne1-gen4-2026.title: NEURA and TUM open Munich RoboGym and unveil 4NE1 Gen 4
neura-tum-robogym-opening-4ne1-gen4-2026.summary: The 2,300-plus-square-meter center combines industrial tasks, robot experience, human demonstrations and simulation.

sections.heading: A research and training center at LabCampus
paragraphs: NEURA Robotics and TUM opened RoboGym near Munich Airport on October 22, spanning more than 2,300 square meters. The initial three-year initiative involves about €17 million, including roughly €11 million from NEURA. Partners from over ten industries began training workflows in September.

sections.heading: Three complementary data streams
paragraphs: Robot sensors record physical tasks; people provide demonstrations through sensing suits, motion capture and teleoperation; simulation and Data Amplifier add variations before validation on hardware. Example tasks include box handling, bottle filling and loading wooden components.

sections.heading: New hardware operating in training facilities
paragraphs: The accompanying 4NE1 Gen 4 has a slimmer body that NEURA says is 20% lighter, a sensorized exterior and locally responding Smart Limbs. It runs Neuron AI and is being prepared for series production. Training-center operation is not a published benchmark or a general customer delivery date.

esab-robbi-ai-adaptive-welding-cobot-lau.title: ESAB introduces ROBBI AI for adaptive cobot welding
esab-robbi-ai-adaptive-welding-cobot-lau.summary: The system generates weld paths and adapts to joints within procedure limits, using local computing at the factory.

sections.heading: Generating paths instead of teaching every point
paragraphs: ESAB detailed ROBBI AI for MIG and TIG on October 22. Operators position it near a joint and supply materials, consumables, weld type and WPS parameters. Sensing identifies the joint and generates a path, targeting low-volume, high-mix work and variable fit-up.

sections.heading: Adaptation inside procedure limits
paragraphs: ESAB says AI can adjust travel, oscillation and welding parameters as gaps change, or stop on conditions that threaten quality. InduSuite helps constrain decisions to specified procedures and qualification requirements. Operators can also disable full-AI mode for conventional cobot use.

sections.heading: Local data and application validation
paragraphs: Simulation precedes deployment, while weld data and video collected onsite support defect review. Computing stays at the facility without requiring continuous cloud communication. Claimed capabilities still need validation against customer materials and WPS; the announcement does not replace application-specific quality inspection.

hirebotics-iphone-smart-teach-painter-la.title: Hirebotics brings iPhone spatial teaching to Cobot Painter
hirebotics-iphone-smart-teach-painter-la.summary: Smart Teach records phone positions and orientations so Beacon can generate editable painting paths.

sections.heading: Teaching around the physical workpiece
paragraphs: Hirebotics introduced updated Smart Teach at FABTECH on October 22. Operators move an iPhone around a part and capture positions and orientations, allowing Beacon to generate a paint path without code or a CAD model. This supplements physically guiding a cobot through individual points.

sections.heading: Reaching awkward surfaces
paragraphs: A small phone can capture points behind, beside or inside large and complex parts more easily than moving the full robot arm. Operators can review generated paths and adjust points, spray parameters and other settings. Programs still need application review rather than automatic acceptance of coating quality.

sections.heading: Painting first, other processes later
paragraphs: Cobot Painter is the first target, with the required iPhone supplied with the system. Cobot Welder and Cobot Cutter are future expansion plans. No measured teaching-time comparison or supported-phone list was provided. The article mentions a video but supplies no clip URL.

hfr-foley-tile-355m-three-year-contract-.summary: The three-year agreement charges by installed area while skilled workers handle cutting, edges, finishing and quality.

sections.heading: A contract for contractor expansion
paragraphs: Human Friendly Robotics announced a three-year, $3.55 million agreement with Foley Tile on October 22. Tyler robots will accompany installers in Arizona and beyond, aiming to let the Tucson crew take larger distant projects without depending as heavily on local recruitment.

sections.heading: Robots place tiles, installers retain skilled work
paragraphs: Tyler handles repetitive placement involving lifting, bending and kneeling. Installers retain cuts, edges, finishing and quality control. Pricing is per installed square foot without an equipment purchase, shifting the contractor’s model toward service-based delivery.

sections.heading: Pilot performance is company-reported
paragraphs: The release says Tyler and the crew at Puerto Rico’s Plaza Las Américas achieved eight times the stated human benchmark pace. It does not detail measurement methods or guarantee every site’s results. This Foley Tile agreement is distinct from the previously announced Flooring Concepts of NJ deal.

sections.heading: Funding industrial expansion
paragraphs: Portuguese unmanned-aircraft developer Beyond Vision raised over €28 million, according to an October 22 report. Índico Capital Partners and Lince Capital co-led, with existing investor ActiveCap participating. The company employs 150 people and serves civilian and military customers.

sections.heading: Hardware with cloud management
paragraphs: Founded in 2013, Beyond Vision moved from software into AI-powered drones and cloud-based management. Funding will strengthen operations and manufacturing while supporting algorithm research and new management-platform functions for security and critical-infrastructure monitoring.

sections.heading: Capacity targets remain unspecified
paragraphs: The NATO-registered supplier plans further international expansion, but the report gives no annual drone-production target, new order total or funding allocation breakdown. Financing supports the expansion plan; it does not establish that manufacturing goals have already been achieved.

korber-naise-strategic-stake-fleet-manag.title: Körber takes a stake in NAiSE for mixed-fleet orchestration
korber-naise-strategic-stake-fleet-manag.summary: The partnership deepens warehouse fleet integration while NAiSE remains independent and open to other manufacturers.

sections.heading: An existing collaboration becomes an investment
paragraphs: Körber announced a stake in NAiSE on October 22 to expand intralogistics fleet-management software. Founded in 2017, NAiSE had been self-funded. The deal deepens an existing collaboration, without disclosing investment size or ownership percentage.

sections.heading: A common layer for mixed vehicles
paragraphs: The platform connects AGVs, AMRs from multiple vendors and manually driven industrial trucks through a shared control layer. Integration with WMS, WES and WCS supports coordinated material flow instead of isolated vendor-specific fleets.

sections.heading: Independence and future applications
paragraphs: NAiSE’s founders retain operational management and the company remains open to other integrators and vehicle manufacturers. The partners plan deeper Körber warehouse integration and future humanoid use cases. That roadmap is not an announcement of an operational commercial humanoid fleet.

lg-innotek-nvidia-hsb-sensing-collaborat.title: LG Innotek and NVIDIA collaborate on direct sensor-to-GPU connectivity
lg-innotek-nvidia-hsb-sensing-collaborat.summary: A 3-megapixel camera and Multimodal Vision System use Holoscan Sensor Bridge, with robot vision and hands on the roadmap.

sections.heading: Sensing products shown in Berlin
paragraphs: LG Innotek announced the NVIDIA collaboration on October 22 after presenting a 3-megapixel camera and Multimodal Vision System at GTC Berlin on October 20. The products are designed around Holoscan Sensor Bridge for robot and machine sensing.

sections.heading: Shortening the data path
paragraphs: HSB uses an open Ethernet-connected fabric to send sensor data to GPU-based AI computing without routing it through the CPU. LG Innotek brings camera, lidar and radar capabilities to the work. The goal is a shorter sensing-to-inference path, but no measured latency was disclosed.

sections.heading: Vision and hands remain expansion plans
paragraphs: The companies plan further humanoid vision-sensing and robotic-hand work, with additional systems to be shown at CES and GTC in 2027. Pricing and delivery schedules were not specified. Planned hand-related work should not be treated as a finished product available today.

enact-30m-preseed-force-assembly-launch-.title: Enact raises $30M to build force-aware assembly robots
enact-30m-preseed-force-assembly-launch-.summary: The Zurich startup combines actuators, control and AI for small-batch assembly, with quantitative performance results still undisclosed.

sections.heading: Funding hardware and AI together
paragraphs: Enact Intelligence has emerged with a $30 million pre-seed round co-led by redalpine and Notion Capital. Founded in Zurich in March 2026 by former 1X and Physical Intelligence engineer Manuel Yves Galliker, it is developing actuators, control systems and models together.

sections.heading: Contact feedback for assembly
paragraphs: The intended robot would use forces during movement to judge whether connectors or seals have seated correctly. Learning from demonstrations targets varied, small-batch work that otherwise needs repeated programming. The company briefing says this approach does not require added artificial skin.

sections.heading: Commercial evidence is still missing
paragraphs: Enact says its first motors exist, but has not disclosed accuracy, success rates, cycle times, pricing or delivery dates. Measuring force over 1,000 times per second and reducing training from months to days remain development targets, not demonstrated production performance.

sections.heading: One goal, different action sequences
paragraphs: Announced on October 22, Physical Reasoning is AGIBOT WORLD 2026 Release 4. Restocking a minibar with three full bottles requires identifying empty bottles, counting existing stock and deciding what to add or remove instead of replaying a fixed motion sequence.

sections.heading: Annotations connect intent and execution
paragraphs: The data links questions, answers, high-level instructions, subtasks and action trajectories. Labels describe objects, locations, arm roles, gripper states and expected outcomes. Nine reasoning categories and three difficulty levels include erroneous examples for studying mistake detection and recovery.

sections.heading: A research resource with conditions
paragraphs: AGIBOT says it is using the data for an upcoming agent framework and model, but reports neither a Release 4 episode count nor measured success-rate gains. everoyal-robot-enclosure-pilot-productio.title: Everoyal reports pilot production of robot enclosures
everoyal-robot-enclosure-pilot-productio.summary: The Suzhou supplier describes roughly 60-unit revisions and combined casting, machining, printing and sheet-metal processes.

sections.heading: Moving beyond display parts
paragraphs: Suzhou Everoyal Precision says its humanoid and service-robot enclosure work has moved into pilot production, typically around 60 units per revision. Its October 23 announcement describes a batch size, not sales or deliveries of complete robots.

sections.heading: Processes under one roof
paragraphs: The company reports a 10,000-square-meter facility with two lines and over 50 machines covering vacuum casting, CNC machining, 3D printing, sheet metal and rapid tooling. Covers, mounting faces and brackets can move between processes without changing suppliers.

sections.heading: Inspection and remaining unknowns
paragraphs: Everoyal says prototypes and machined parts receive 100% inspection using Zeiss CMM and ROMER equipment, with reports. Batch work uses 5% random inspection at an agreed depth. Customers, delivery schedules and independent results are undisclosed, so these remain supplier-reported capabilities.

advantech-five-layer-independent-safety-.title: Advantech separates robot safety from AI in a five-layer platform
advantech-five-layer-independent-safety-.summary: Its IGX Thor-based MIC-735-IT supports an optional Safety MCU and engineering evidence; final system certification remains application-specific.

sections.heading: A platform spanning the robot lifecycle
paragraphs: Advantech presents five layers: perception, AI computing and motion control, functional safety, production and validation, and deployment and management. The architecture aims to help robot builders integrate hardware, software and validation evidence.

sections.heading: An independent safety path
paragraphs: AI computation is separated from health monitoring and fault detection to support application-defined safe states. The NVIDIA IGX Thor-based MIC-735-IT can include a Renesas Safety MCU. Diagnostics, a safety manual and FMEDA-related evidence support engineering work.

sections.heading: System certification remains specific
paragraphs: Support for standards such as IEC 61508 and ISO 13849 does not certify every robot built on the platform. Integrators or customers remain responsible for hazard analysis, integration, validation and final certification. Advantech plans demonstrations at NVIDIA GTC Berlin.

kabam-november20-closure-announcement-20.title: Kabam Robotics plans November 20 shutdown after six years
kabam-november20-closure-announcement-20.summary: Customers have reportedly been notified as executives consider an AI-focused direction; arrangements for deployed robots remain to be clarified.

sections.heading: Customers notified ahead of closure
paragraphs: VnExpress, citing The Business Times, reports that Singapore’s Kabam Robotics emailed customers about a November 20 shutdown and asked them to resolve outstanding matters beforehand. Founded under Patec in 2020, Kabam merged with Cognicept Systems in 2022.

sections.heading: Deployments did not remove business pressure
paragraphs: Its patrol, surveillance and inspection robots served customers including Changi Airport Group, Certis and Aetos. The report cites over 150 deployments as of 2023, not a current count. Patec attributed the decision to production costs and market conditions despite industry awards.

sections.heading: Staff and service arrangements remain open
paragraphs: A co-founder confirmed closure to Lianhe Zaobao and discussed shifting from hardware toward AI. A new company and some staff transfers were still under discussion. The affected workforce count and support arrangements for installed robots remain unclear.

warp-sciences-wetlab-215m-launch-2026.title: Warp Sciences launches with $215M to automate wet labs
warp-sciences-wetlab-215m-launch-2026.summary: Kevin Weil’s startup plans to train robots through chemists wearing cameras and sensor gloves; operational results remain undisclosed.

sections.heading: A new venture for Kevin Weil
paragraphs: Former OpenAI science lead Kevin Weil has announced Warp Sciences. TechCrunch reports $215 million raised at an $865 million valuation, citing his announcement. Lightspeed led, joined by IVP, Mayfield, Lux, Premji and Menlo.

sections.heading: Teaching physical laboratory work
paragraphs: Chemists wearing cameras and sensor gloves would train robots to synthesize and test compounds selected by researchers. The focus is physical wet-lab work supporting drug discovery rather than generating text-only research suggestions.

sections.heading: Targets still need operational proof
paragraphs: Warp aims for continuous operation and domestic synthesis capacity that reduces reliance on overseas contractors. The report gives no daily throughput, accuracy figures or service-launch date, so faster drug development remains an objective rather than a demonstrated outcome.

sections.heading: Two financing components
paragraphs: FORT announced about $20 million in commitments on October 22: roughly $10 million led by Tiger Global with Mark Cuban Companies, expected to close that week, and another $10 million Tiger PIPE commitment tied to the Newbury Street II merger.

sections.heading: Resources for deployment
paragraphs: FORT plans to expand staffing and operating capacity. It reports over 19,500 safety-system units across more than 600 customers; these are company figures, not new robots manufactured with this financing.

sections.heading: Listing remains conditional
paragraphs: The expected Nasdaq symbol FROB depends on merger completion and approvals. This financing development is separate from the previously covered connectivity-software launch and does not confirm a completed public listing.

maxinsights-30m-seed-maxloop-maxglove-20.title: Maxinsights raises $30M and introduces MaxLoop and MaxGlove
maxinsights-30m-seed-maxloop-maxglove-20.summary: It reports 1.5 million model-ready hours from over 2 million captured hours; its million-hour force-data goal is for 2027.

sections.heading: Capturing everyday work
paragraphs: Maxinsights announced a $30 million seed round led by Peak XV on October 22. It pays over 5,000 collectors to record real tasks such as cooking and cleaning, reporting more than 2 million captured hours, including 1.5 million model-ready hours. These are company figures.

sections.heading: Quality checks and contact data
paragraphs: MaxLoop scores incoming recordings and feeds guidance back to collectors. MaxGlove, developed with Genesis AI, captures touch and force, including grip and object-weight information that video alone cannot reveal.

sections.heading: Separating inventory from targets
paragraphs: One million hours of force data in 2027 is a target, not delivered inventory. Data volume does not establish better robot success rates. This report uses the accessible Business Wire syndication on MarketMinute; the direct Business Wire page could not be inspected during this run.
